questions.question: What’s the difference between pretending to listen and only picking what you want to hear? Why are both bad when working in teams? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What’s the difference between
  • pretending to listen and only
  • picking what you want to hear?
  • Why are both bad when
  • working in teams?
  • Pretending to listen means acting as if one is listening while
  • actually ignoring the message, whereas selective listening means
  • hearing only the parts that match one’s interests or opinions.
  • Both are harmful in teams because they cause
  • misunderstandings, reduce trust, and prevent effective
  • collaboration and decision-making.

questions.question: What should be included and how should you write a letter if you want to complain about something, and what is a “call to action?” / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What should be included and
  • how should you write a letter if
  • you want to complain about
  • something, and what is a “call
  • to action”?

  • recipient’s address, subject, salutation, clear explanation of the
  • problem, supporting details, and a polite request for a solution.
  • The tone should be formal and respectful. A call to action is a
  • clear request asking the recipient to take specific steps to resolve
  • the issue.

questions.question: Discuss the various external and internal pressures (e.g., globalization, hierarchy, technology) that complicate the decoding process for a message receiver in a large corporation (CO1, CO5). / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the various external and
  • internal pressures (e.g., globalization,
  • hierarchy, technology) that
  • complicate the decoding process for a
  • message receiver in a large
  • corporation.
  • In large corporations, several factors affect how messages
  • are interpreted. Globalization introduces language
  • differences and cultural variations that may alter meaning.
  • Hierarchy can distort messages as information passes
  • through multiple organizational levels. Technology such as
  • emails, messaging platforms, and virtual meetings may
  • remove tone and non-verbal cues, causing
  • misunderstanding. Internal pressures like workload, stress,
  • and organizational politics may also influence how a
  • receiver interprets a message. These factors make accurate
  • decoding challenging and require clear communication
  • practices.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the effect of posture, gestures, and facial expressions on communication. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the effect of posture,
  • gestures, and facial expressions on
  • communication.
  • Posture, gestures, and facial expressions are important
  • aspects of non-verbal communication. Good posture
  • conveys confidence and professionalism, while appropriate
  • gestures help emphasize ideas and make communication
  • more engaging. Facial expressions express emotions and
  • attitudes, helping listeners understand the speaker’s
  • feelings. Positive non-verbal signals strengthen the
  • message, while negative signals such as crossed arms or
  • frowning may create misunderstanding or reduce credibility.

questions.question: Write an essay on strategies to accept criticism positively? / [CO4] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on strategies to accept criticism positively.
  • Accepting criticism positively is an important
  • communication and personal development skill. Strategies
  • include listening carefully without interrupting, staying calm
  • and avoiding defensive reactions, and trying to understand
  • the intention behind the feedback. Asking questions for
  • clarification can help improve understanding. It is also
  • important to evaluate criticism objectively and identify
  • useful suggestions for improvement. Showing appreciation
  • for constructive feedback helps build professional
  • relationships. Finally, using criticism as an opportunity for
  • learning and self-improvement can lead to personal and
  • professional growth.
